nodes.label: Ownership and control
nodes.title: The ban covers taxes on **ownership or control**, including indirectly held assets.

quotes.text:
may enact, create,
impose, or authorize collection of a tax on the ownership
or control of retirement holdings, individually owned
assets, and other forms of personal savings, whether
held directly or indirectly.

nodes.label: Existing taxes retained
nodes.title: The ownership-tax restriction preserves qualifying **existing taxes**.

quotes.text:
Nothing in this section shall alter or limit the
imposition or collection of any tax that was in effect,
imposed, and first collected on or before December 31,
2025.

nodes.label: Real property unchanged
nodes.title: The ownership-tax section leaves **real property taxation** unchanged.

quotes.text:
taxation of real property as provided in other provisions

of this Constitution.

nodes.label: Beyond retirement accounts
nodes.title: Covered assets include **business interests** and personal belongings.

quotes.text:
investment accounts, business interests, digital assets,
                                                                   
      intellectual property, personal belongings, and other
      assets used to produce or collect income or savings for

nodes.label: Past residency
nodes.title: The retroactive-tax restriction expressly covers **past residency status**.

quotes.text:
This subdivision also applies to a tax that is imposed
on a taxpayer based upon their residency status on a
date prior to the effective date of the tax.

nodes.label: Emergency exception limit
nodes.title: The legislative emergency exception limits retroactivity to **365 days**.

quotes.text:
The tax does not apply retroactively for more than       
      365 days prior to the date the statute takes effect.

nodes.label: Fiscal emergency condition
nodes.title: The exception requires emergency revenue to fund the **declared fiscal emergency**.

quotes.text:
The Governor declares a fiscal emergency pursuant        
      to subdivision (f) of Section 10 of Article IV and the use   
      of the revenues from the tax are expressly limited by the    
      statute to responding to the fiscal emergency.

nodes.label: Effective and operative
nodes.title: The act becomes operative **when it takes effect** under the Constitution.

quotes.text:
This act shall take effect at the earliest possible date in
accordance with Section 10 of Article II of the California
Constitution. This act shall become operative on the
same day it takes effect.

nodes.label: Conflicting ballot measures
nodes.title: Its conflict clause can nullify **another measure in full** if Prop 42 receives more affirmative votes.

quotes.text:
prevail in their entirety, and all the provisions of the     
      other measure shall be null and void.

nodes.label: Authors' planning rationale
nodes.title: The authors say **advance notice** is needed for financial planning.

quotes.text:
can make decisions with advance notice of what the            
      rules are.

nodes.label: Current financial-asset taxes
nodes.title: The Analyst distinguishes **asset income** from simply owning financial assets.

quotes.locator: BACKGROUND, Ownership of Financial Assets Is Not Taxed, final sentence
quotes.text: Although the state does tax income people make from their financial assets, there is no tax for simply owning those assets.

nodes.label: Uncertain future revenue
nodes.title: The Analyst says **future revenue reductions** are possible but unclear.

quotes.locator: FISCAL EFFECTS, Possibility That Tax Revenues Will Be Lower in the Future
quotes.text: This could reduce future tax revenues. When and by how much future revenues would be reduced is unclear.

nodes.label: Courts and Prop 40
nodes.title: The Analyst says **Prop 40 could be stopped**, depending on vote totals and a court finding.

quotes.locator: Potential Interactions With Other Propositions, paragraph 1
quotes.text: If Proposition 42 receives more “yes” votes than Proposition 40 on this same ballot, then Proposition 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters. This is because the courts could find that Proposition 42 conflicts with Proposition 40.

nodes.label: Supporters' savings rationale
nodes.title: Supporters argue that **ownership taxes** would tax already-earned money again.

quotes.locator: ARGUMENT IN FAVOR, CALIFORNIA CONSTITUTION CURRENTLY ALLOWS DOUBLE TAXATION, paragraph 1
quotes.text: This means politicians can tax the same money twice: once when you earn it, and again when it is sitting in your retirement funds or savings accounts.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Michael Hedges, President California Small Business Association; Shelley Huff, Commander AMVETS, Department of California; Jennifer Yoder, Board Member California Senior Alliance

nodes.label: Supporters' predictable rules
nodes.title: Supporters argue that **stable rules** protect retirement planning.

quotes.locator: ARGUMENT IN FAVOR, PROP. 42 PROHIBITS UNFAIR RETROACTIVE TAXES, quoted statement
quotes.text: People plan their retirement for years—they deserve stable, predictable rules that don’t change after years of saving and planning.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Michael Hedges, President California Small Business Association; Shelley Huff, Commander AMVETS, Department of California; Jennifer Yoder, Board Member California Senior Alliance

nodes.label: Opponents' healthcare concern
nodes.title: Opponents connect blocking **the billionaire tax** to healthcare funding.

quotes.locator: ARGUMENT AGAINST, PROP. 42 WOULD CANCEL OUT THE BILLIONAIRE TAX, paragraph 2
quotes.text: It’s about preventing one specific tax that billionaires want to avoid, because they’d rather millions of working people lose healthcare than pay a modest, one-time tax on their extreme wealth.

attribution.name: Ballot argument against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Opponents' funding allegation
nodes.title: Opponents allege that **billionaire funding** explains the measure's purpose.

quotes.locator: REBUTTAL TO ARGUMENT IN FAVOR, PROP. 42 WOULD CANCEL OUT THE BILLIONAIRE TAX, paragraph 1
quotes.text: Prop. 42 is a billionaire-funded scheme designed specifically to undo the California Billionaire Tax, Prop. 40.

attribution.name: Rebuttal against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Supporters' broad protection
nodes.title: Supporters describe **comprehensive constitutional protection**, not just a response to one tax.

quotes.locator: REBUTTAL TO ARGUMENT AGAINST, CALIFORNIA IS EXPENSIVE ENOUGH WITHOUT DOUBLE TAXATION, final sentence
quotes.text: It is a comprehensive constitutional protection against politicians or special interests trying to tax our retirement funds and savings accounts.

attribution.name: Rebuttal for

nodes.label: Ownership versus earnings
nodes.title: Separate taxes on **ownership** from taxes on income earned from assets.
nodes.body: The Analyst's distinction helps identify what the ownership-tax ban addresses. It does not describe an end to taxation of investment income.

edges.why: The Analyst distinguishes a possible future ownership tax from taxes currently imposed on asset income.
The proposed law allows limited legislative retroactivity under emergency conditions.
The Analyst identifies a possible revenue effect but does not quantify resulting service changes.
The Analyst describes a conditional legal interaction rather than certain cancellation.
The related measure also asserts priority over conflicting provisions.
The measure preserves qualifying preexisting taxes rather than abolishing all personal-property taxes.
Past residency is expressly included in the retroactivity restriction relevant to evaluating other tax measures.
